text.p: Israel began work on a Jewish hilltop settlement on the outskirts of Arab East Jerusalem on Tuesday, reigniting the struggle with Palestinians over the fate of the holy city.

THE DISPUTE. Israel plans to build 6,500 houses for Jews on a hilltop it calls Har Homa, aiming to complete a ring of Jewish neighbourhoods around East Jerusalem that would cement its claim to the city as Israel's "eternal, undivided" capital.
Palestinians, who call the hill Jabal Abu Ghneim, say the housing project would be a barrier between nearby Arab towns and Arab neighbourhoods in East Jerusalem.

Israel captured East Jerusalem from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East War and its claim to the city is disputed by most of the world. Palestinians want East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future state.

THE PEACE CONTEXT. Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu, the right-wing Likud party leader elected prime minister 10 months ago on a promise to get tough in negotiations with the Arabs, says peace deals with the Palestinians do not bar construction of new settlements. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat counters that the unilateral housing project breaches accords that make Jerusalem a subject for negotiation in "final status" talks due to have resumed this week and run until May 1999.

POPULATION. Israel has built housing for Jews in East Jerusalem since 1967 so that a nearly equal number of Jews and Arabs -- 160,000 apiece -- now live there. About 70 percent of East and West Jerusalem's 584,000 residents are Jews.

HOLY SITES. The city sacred to Christians, Jews and Moslems is home to dozens of shrines. Three of these -- situated in East Jerusalem's walled Old City -- are the traditional burial place of Jesus at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, the Wailing Wall that is a remnant of the retaining wall of Judaism's ancient temple, and al-Haram al-Sharif (the Noble Sanctuary), Islam's most important site apart from Mecca and Medina.
HISTORY. Jerusalem, built on the Judean hills, traces its history back at least 4,000 years. The biblical King David made Jerusalem his capital when he conquered the city about 3,000 years ago.

Christians, Moslems and Jews have lived in Jerusalem from the time of the Moslem conquest in 638. The history of West Jerusalem began in 1860 with the building of Jewish quarters outside the walls of the Old City.

The United Nations 1947 resolution dividing British-run Palestine into Arab and Jewish states recommended Jerusalem become a separate international entity under U.N. trusteeship. But a plan for internationalising Jerusalem was rejected by both Arabs and Jews and not approved by the United Nations.

The British left and Israel proclaimed statehood on May 14, 1948, igniting a war with the Arabs. Jordan took control of predominantly Arab East Jerusalem, including the Old City, two weeks later and held onto it until Israel captured it during the Six Day War in June 1967.

Israel later annexed it to West Jerusalem against the will of its Arab inhabitants who refused to take Israeli citizenship. Palestinians of the West Bank and Gaza Strip complain Israeli army closures, imposed for security reasons, bar them from entering the city to reach holy sites.
